s:
Consider the following statements about poverty in 2011-12 (Tendulkar method):
1. Andaman and Nicobar Islands had the lowest poverty ratio (1.00%).
2. Chhattisgarh had the highest poverty ratio (39.93%).
3. Bihar had the largest number of poor people.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct (Goa, 5.09%, was the lowest State). 3 is wrong: Uttar Pradesh had the largest number of poor, about 5.98 crore; Bihar had 3.58 crore.

s:
Consider the following statements about the RBI's update of the Rangarajan poverty line (HCES 2022-23):
1. Chhattisgarh had the highest rural poverty, at 25.1%.
2. Chhattisgarh also had the highest urban poverty.
3. Himachal Pradesh had the lowest rural poverty.
4. Kerala had the lowest urban poverty.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct (Chhattisgarh rural 25.1%, urban 13.3%; HP rural 0.4%). Statement 4 is wrong: the lowest urban poverty was in Tamil Nadu (1.9%).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. As per the National MPI (NFHS-5, 2019-21), Bihar has the highest and Kerala the lowest multidimensional poverty.
2. Uttar Pradesh recorded the largest number of people (5.94 crore) exiting multidimensional poverty between 2013-14 and 2022-23.
3. Between 2011-12 and 2022-23, rural poverty in Bihar fell from 47.8% to 8.6%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the 47.8% → 8.6% fall in rural poverty was Odisha's; Bihar's figure is urban poverty, 50.8% → 9.1% – high-poverty States fell fastest.

s:
Match List-I (Estimate, Tendulkar line) with List-II (Poverty ratio):
List-I | List-II
a. All-India, 2009-10 | i. 2.3%
b. Rural India, 2011-12 | ii. 25.7%
c. Urban India, 2011-12 | iii. 29.8%
d. All-India, 2023-24 (updated line, Economic Survey 2025-26) | iv. 13.7%
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Tendulkar: 29.8% all-India in 2009-10; 2011-12 rural 25.7%, urban 13.7% (total 21.9%); updated line 4.7% (2022-23) and 2.3% (2023-24).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the MDGs, India's target was to halve poverty from 47.8% in 1990 to 23.9% by 2015.
2. India met the MDG target of halving extreme poverty.
3. World Bank $3-a-day extreme poverty in India fell from 27.1% in 2011-12 to 2.3% in 2022-23.
4. The national multidimensional poverty headcount fell from 55.3% (2005-06) to 14.96% (2019-21).
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct (India missed hunger, maternal health and sanitation targets; MPI was 11.28% by 2022-23). Statement 3 is wrong: the $3-a-day figure fell to 5.3% in 2022-23; 2.3% is the updated Tendulkar-line poverty of 2023-24.

Match List-I (Andhra Pradesh body / project) with List-II (Feature):
List-I | List-II
a. SERP | i. Set up in 2000 to mobilise the rural poor into women's SHGs
b. Velugu | ii. World Bank-aided District Poverty Initiatives Project
c. Indira Kranthi Patham | iii. Urban SHGs, set up in 2007
d. MEPMA | iv. Velugu and DWCRA merged (2004-05)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: SERP (2000) – social mobilisation of the rural poor; Velugu (2000) – World Bank-aided District Poverty Initiatives Project run by SERP; IKP (2004-05) – Velugu and DWCRA merged; MEPMA (1 Sep 2007) – urban SHGs.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Andhra Pradesh Mahila Sadhikara Samstha (APMSS) works for poor households in both rural and urban areas.
Reason (R): SERP works in rural areas while MEPMA works in urban areas.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: SERP = rural, MEPMA = urban, APMSS = both. But R only describes the two other bodies; it does not explain why APMSS covers both areas (it is the integrated body).

s:
Consider the following statements about poverty in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Under the Tendulkar method (2011-12), AP's rural and urban poverty ratios were 10.96% and 5.81%.
2. AP's poverty ratio under the Tendulkar method was 44.6% in 1993-94.
3. AP's poverty ratio under the Tendulkar method was 15.8% in 2004-05.
4. AP's multidimensional poverty headcount (2019-21) was 6.06%.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: AP's Tendulkar figure for 2004-05 was 29.9% (then 21.1% in 2009-10 and 9.20% in 2011-12); 15.8% is the old official URP estimate of the Eleventh Plan.

s:
Consider the following statements about regional poverty in Andhra Pradesh (MPI, old 13 districts):
1. Vizianagaram had the highest MPI poverty headcount.
2. West Godavari had the lowest MPI poverty headcount (2.42%).
3. Rayalaseema is poorer mainly because of its dependence on rain-fed agriculture.
4. The delta districts are generally the least poor.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct (delta districts gain from irrigation and productivity). Statement 1 is wrong: the poorest district was Kurnool (12.84%); Vizianagaram was next (8.66%).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): In 2011-12, Andhra Pradesh's urban poverty ratio was higher than the all-India urban poverty ratio.
Reason (R): Andhra Pradesh's work participation rate is higher than India's.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: in 2011-12 both rural (10.96%) and urban (5.81%) poverty in AP were below the all-India levels (25.70% / 13.70%). R is true.

Match List-I (Cause of regional poverty difference) with List-II (Effect):
List-I | List-II
a. Agricultural productivity and irrigation | i. PMGKAY, MGNREGA and PMAY-G cut poverty
b. Infrastructure and investment | ii. Low education leads to higher poverty
c. Human capital | iii. Investment only in select locales
d. Social transfers | iv. Delta gains while rain-fed Rayalaseema lags
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Productivity and irrigation – delta vs Rayalaseema; infrastructure and investment – select locales; human capital – low education, higher poverty; social transfers – PMGKAY, MGNREGA, PMAY-G.

Consider the following statements about recent anti-poverty measures:
1. Bihar runs the Satat Jeevikoparjan Yojana, a graduation-approach model.
2. The Samaveshi Aajeevika Yojana is run by the Centre under DAY-NRLM.
3. Kerala is moving to extreme-poverty-free status.
4. The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 raised the rural job guarantee to 150 days.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the VB-G RAM G Act (passed 18 Dec 2025) guarantees 125 days.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Scheduled Tribes have the highest poverty ratio among social groups (about 43-45% in 2011-12).
2. About 35.1% of persons with no formal education are poor, against 14.9% of those with post-secondary education.
3. India's social protection coverage rose from 22% in 2016 to 64.3% in 2025.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three are correct as per the notes (SCs follow STs at about 29%).
